channel.title: Cobble Updates
channel.description: Signed Full releases of Cobble for macOS.

item.description:
Full Cobble browser for Apple silicon and macOS 26+.
- New Keyboard Privacy setting (Settings → Browsing, off by default). When on, websites no longer see ⌘ or ⌃ keys in WebKit and Chromium tabs or in page full screen, not even when held while typing other keys, moving the pointer or scrolling. Clicks still report them so ⌘-click and ⌃-click work. Cobble shortcuts, copy/paste and text editing keys such as ⌘← or ⌃A keep working; site shortcuts such as ⌘K stop, and Monaco code editors in Chromium tabs lose ⌘-arrow and ⌘⌫. - Clicking Cobble in the Dock brings back your window, even when it's minimized or still opening, instead of adding a second one. New windows open only from New Window: ⌘N, the File menu, or the Dock icon's menu. ⌘T from Settings opens the tab in your existing window.
Includes WebKit, Chromium and signed in-app updates. Uses the pinned public ABI 18 SDK (371054c) and its matching Chromium runtime.
This is an early beta. Real-site camera and microphone behavior, interrupted download recovery, real-account authentication, clean-Mac installation and installed version-to-version updates remain unqualified.
Download the ZIP, extract Cobble, quit the old app and replace it in Applications. Beta 1 users need one manual install because that version's updater cannot start.

Full Cobble browser for Apple silicon and macOS 26+.
- The site menu is simpler: connection status at the top (click it for the certificate), then on/off switches for Camera, Microphone, Sound and Pop-ups. Allowing camera or microphone now always remembers the site, so the switch stays on until you turn it off. Turning it off also stops the camera or microphone on that page. Works in WebKit and Chromium tabs. - Native window buttons appear when a window enters full screen.

Full Cobble browser for Apple silicon and macOS 26+.
- Video and page full screen works in Chromium tabs. YouTube and other sites open in their own full-screen Space with a brief "Press Esc to exit" banner. Esc, the site's own button or leaving the Space returns the page to its tab. - A crashed Chromium page no longer quits the whole browser.
